answer: Assay-of-latent-cache mechanism.** Each new agent identity must surface a randomly drawn batch of cached query answers only the live network holds, scored against a grove of peer-verified reference outputs. To pass, a sybil must actually operate a persistent inference cache, since the probing schedule sits at the zenith of adaptive difficulty. The cost is a full sustained serving footprint per identity plus karst-like gradual cache erosion from continuous probing, making mass fake agents costlier than honest ones.
